tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Fredholm alternative for the Dirichlet problem] 1. ch6:6.15\group gt-ch06 Let $L$ be strictly elliptic with $C^\alpha (\bar\Omega )$ coefficients on a $C^{2,\alpha }$ domain. Either the homogeneous Dirichlet problem has only the zero solution, in which case the inhomogeneous problem has a unique $C^{2,\alpha }(\bar\Omega )$ solution for every admissible $(f,\varphi )$, or its homogeneous solution space is finite dimensional.
Proof

\sketch Restrict $L$ to $\mathbb B=\{ u\in C^{2,\alpha }(\bar\Omega ):u=0\text{ on } \partial \Omega \} $. For $\sigma \ge \sup c$, $L-\sigma $ is invertible by Theorem 6.14 and its inverse is compact on $C^\alpha (\bar\Omega )$. The equation

\begin{equation} \tag {6.46} u+\sigma (L-\sigma )^{-1}u=(L-\sigma )^{-1}f \end{equation}

is therefore covered by the Fredholm alternative. Applying $L-\sigma $ gives the equivalent boundary problem

\begin{equation} \tag {6.47} Lu=f,\qquad u\in \mathbb B. \end{equation}

This yields the two cases.

□
